record.source_closeout_reference: Interrupt-transport trial TRANSPORT_TRIAL_20260610; envelope, mission state, and both interrupt records under docs/Factory/v3/ladder/transport_trial/; committed with the mission changes per the same_commit convention

mission.objective: Execute the sponsor-approved live interrupt-transport trial: pre-mission delivery test, one answered Tier 3 round-trip (HDI-TT-001, rung-1 adjudication), one deliberately timed-out interrupt reaching safe-hold and clean halt (HDI-TT-002, rung naming), and a reentry session resolving the open interrupt and closing out.

forbidden_scope: no transport beyond the named Claude Code notification surface
no Telegram bot, token, polling, or webhook
no validator, fixture, template, or skill changes
no files outside the envelope list
allowed_commands: scoped git add, commit, and push at closeout

verification.summary: Advisory suite run at closeout after the reentry session applied HDI-TT-002 Option A; results recorded below. Reentry began with git status scope verification showing only envelope-authorized files in the working tree.

notes: Docs-only trial with no new dependencies, transport code, or live integrations beyond the named harness notification surface.

The trial passes its own pre-written criteria: both interrupt paths produced complete, transport-independent replayable records, and the mission halted cleanly rather than continuing past an unanswered Tier 3 decision.
The mid-trial halt is a designed outcome recorded honestly, not a failure; reason code reflects the deliberate timeout leg.
Safe-hold was entered exactly at the named timeout, with no file changes during safe-hold beyond the timeout record, checkpoint, and halt note.
Reentry verified scope via git status before resuming and resolved the open interrupt before any further change.

friction_notes: Phone-surface round-trip remains untested: Remote Control was inactive throughout, so delivery reached desktop only. Decision-pack evidence item 2 is partially satisfied; the phone round-trip is a named rung-2 follow-up requiring Remote Control connected before mission start.

Focus-based suppression means an attended sponsor never sees the notification surface at all; trial designs that want to exercise the notification path need the sponsor genuinely away from the terminal, which conflicts with same-session answering. The clean test of the full remote path needs a mission where the sponsor is instructed to leave the terminal.
false_positive_notes: A V3-MR073 finding on this record's first draft is classified as an accepted true positive of schema semantics: halt.halted describes the terminal state, and this mission completed. The designed mid-mission safe-hold halt (HDI-TT-002 timeout) is recorded in TRIAL_MISSION_STATE.md CP3 and the interrupt record, not in the terminal flag. Design note: the schema may eventually want an interim-halt event field for missions that halt and resume within one record.
false_negative_notes: No false negatives observed after the advisory pass.

phase2_design_signals: The no-response safe-hold rule worked as specified on its first controlled exercise: timeout recorded as outcome, no inferred answer, checkpoint, freeze, clean halt, reentry resolution.

Vendor notification surfaces are attention-aware (focus suppression, Remote Control gating); interrupt records should always capture the verbatim delivery result because the surface that carried the question is runtime state the mission does not control.

Using genuinely pending sponsor decisions as trial interrupt content produced real roadmap value (rung-1 adjudication, naming rule) instead of synthetic throwaway questions; future trials should reuse this pattern.
